findings.rationale: The temporary Markdown materialization is named only by source stem and process ID, then opened with std::fs::write and unconditionally removed on Drop. A preexisting file or two live materializations in one process therefore share a path: one invocation can truncate the other's file, and dropping either state can delete a file still in use (or an unrelated preexisting file). Use an exclusively created, per-invocation temporary file and retain ownership of its handle/path.

The documented raw-block contract names evaluator and failure_mode as accepted, echoed block boundaries, and PROJECT_BLOCKS recognizes them, but RAW_BLOCKS omits both. Since parse_ai_project stores raw declarations only when their kind is in RAW_BLOCKS, these declarations are silently discarded while project checking can still report success.
